title: The Hidden Bag
statement: Bag P and Bag Q each contain $10$ cards, and each card shows one positive integer. In Bag P, exactly $8$ of the cards show odd numbers. One card is drawn at random from each bag, with all cards in a bag equally likely. The probability that the sum of the two numbers drawn is even is $\frac{31}{50}$. How many cards in Bag Q show odd numbers?
hints: Only one feature of each number matters here. For each possible draw, ask whether each card is odd or even, and see what that says about the sum.

Use parity: a sum of two integers is even exactly when both are odd or both are even. Let $k$ be the number of odd cards in Bag Q, and count the pairs of cards, one from each bag, that have an even sum.

Bag Q has $k$ odd cards and $10 - k$ even cards, and Bag P has $8$ odd cards and $2$ even cards. Of the $100$ equally likely pairs, $8k$ are both odd and $2(10 - k)$ are both even. Since $\frac{31}{50}$ of $100$ is $62$, these two counts must add up to $62$.
solution:
Let Bag Q have $k$ odd cards. The sum is even when both cards are odd or both are even, so
$$\dfrac{8k+2(10-k)}{100}=\dfrac{31}{50}.$$
Then $6k+20=62$, so $k=7$.
